evidence: Owner sends to Chief, Manager and Ticket conversations now answer {conversation_id, fate:'accepted', message_id} at durable acceptance instead of waiting for started, queued or injected (Ticket t_8r4xr4q4, pull request 1338). Delivery is reported later through transcript rows and receipts under the same sender_message_id. Installed builds 11 and 12 decode fate as a String and settle every fate except refused and suppressed as sent (Outbox.swift), so a send stays visible and a later prompt_refused or prompt_uncertain row still shows its note. But most refusals now arrive after acceptance, and on those builds a refusal that arrives after the outbox settled the item as sent has no working Try Again. Following the owner rule for client-visible changes, raise MINIMUM_SUPPORTED_BUILD to 13 and set the new app build to 13. Existing HTTP admission refuses builds 11 and 12 with 426 ios_update_required before reads or actions; the existing native latch requests a TestFlight update and retains drafts and outbox work. Build 13 reads accepted, recorded, started, injected and queued as sent; uncertain and unknown fates as sent with the Delivery unconfirmed note and no resend; a refusal after acceptance reopens the item as failed with Try Again under a new sender_message_id and reconciles_sequence; a first message sent without a conversation retries into the current conversation. Additive server fields that build 13 ignores or reads as optional: pending_messages on the conversation read and waiting_messages_revision on view status. The owner-send status route now returns {outcome}; native builds do not call it. View receipts keep their kinds. The desktop shell loads the web app from home and reads no send outcome, so the desktop bridge floor stays 2. Shared Fastify injection refuses builds 9 to 12 for reads and actions with no handler run, and admits build 13. iOS host tests (ios/scripts/test-offline.sh, 242 passed) and hosted Native iOS CI (host suites and unsigned Simulator build) passed on the branch. Not tested: a signed device, TestFlight distribution, or the installed build 12 latch against this server. Matching client releases must be available for this server release; production deployment remains a later owner action.
